# Security

> Learn about Claude Code's security safeguards and best practices for safe usage.

## How we approach security

### Security foundation

Your code's security is paramount. Claude Code is built with security at its core, developed according to Anthropic's comprehensive security program. Learn more and access resources (SOC 2 Type 2 report, ISO 27001 certificate, etc.) at [Anthropic Trust Center](https://trust.anthropic.com).

### Permission-based architecture

Claude Code uses strict read-only permissions by default. When additional actions are needed (editing files, running tests, executing commands), Claude Code requests explicit permission. Users control whether to approve actions once or allow them automatically.

We designed Claude Code to be transparent and secure. For example, we require approval for bash commands before executing them, giving you direct control. This approach enables users and organizations to configure permissions directly.

For detailed permission configuration, see [Permissions](/en/permissions).

### Built-in protections

To mitigate risks in agentic systems:

* **Sandboxed bash tool**: [Sandbox](/en/sandboxing) bash commands with filesystem and network isolation, reducing permission prompts while maintaining security. Enable with `/sandbox` to define boundaries where Claude Code can work autonomously
* **Write access restriction**: Claude Code can only write to the folder where it was started and its subfolders—it cannot modify files in parent directories without explicit permission. While Claude Code can read files outside the working directory (useful for accessing system libraries and dependencies), write operations are strictly confined to the project scope, creating a clear security boundary
* **Prompt fatigue mitigation**: Support for allowlisting frequently used safe commands per-user, per-codebase, or per-organization
* **Accept Edits mode**: Batch accept multiple edits while maintaining permission prompts for commands with side effects

### User responsibility

Claude Code only has the permissions you grant it. You're responsible for reviewing proposed code and commands for safety before approval.

## Protect against prompt injection

Prompt injection is a technique where an attacker attempts to override or manipulate an AI assistant's instructions by inserting malicious text. Claude Code includes several safeguards against these attacks:

### Core protections

* **Permission system**: Sensitive operations require explicit approval
* **Context-aware analysis**: Detects potentially harmful instructions by analyzing the full request
* **Input sanitization**: Prevents command injection by processing user inputs
* **Command blocklist**: Blocks risky commands that fetch arbitrary content from the web like `curl` and `wget` by default. When explicitly allowed, be aware of [permission pattern limitations](/en/permissions#tool-specific-permission-rules)

### Privacy safeguards

We have implemented several safeguards to protect your data, including:

* Limited retention periods for sensitive information (see the [Privacy Center](https://privacy.anthropic.com/en/articles/10023548-how-long-do-you-store-my-data) to learn more)
* Restricted access to user session data
* User control over data training preferences. Consumer users can change their [privacy settings](https://claude.ai/settings/privacy) at any time.

For full details, please review our [Commercial Terms of Service](https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms) (for Team, Enterprise, and API users) or [Consumer Terms](https://www.anthropic.com/legal/consumer-terms) (for Free, Pro, and Max users) and [Privacy Policy](https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy).

### Additional safeguards

* **Network request approval**: Tools that make network requests require user approval by default
* **Isolated context windows**: Web fetch uses a separate context window to avoid injecting potentially malicious prompts
* **Trust verification**: First-time codebase runs and new MCP servers require trust verification
  * Note: Trust verification is disabled when running non-interactively with the `-p` flag
* **Command injection detection**: Suspicious bash commands require manual approval even if previously allowlisted
* **Fail-closed matching**: Unmatched commands default to requiring manual approval
* **Natural language descriptions**: Complex bash commands include explanations for user understanding
* **Secure credential storage**: API keys and tokens are encrypted. See [Credential Management](/en/authentication#credential-management)

<Warning>
  **Windows WebDAV security risk**: When running Claude Code on Windows, we recommend against enabling WebDAV or allowing Claude Code to access paths such as `\\*` that may contain WebDAV subdirectories. [WebDAV has been deprecated by Microsoft](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/whats-new/deprecated-features#:~:text=The%20Webclient%20\(WebDAV\)%20service%20is%20deprecated) due to security risks. Enabling WebDAV may allow Claude Code to trigger network requests to remote hosts, bypassing the permission system.
</Warning>

**Best practices for working with untrusted content**:

1. Review suggested commands before approval
2. Avoid piping untrusted content directly to Claude
3. Verify proposed changes to critical files
4. Use virtual machines (VMs) to run scripts and make tool calls, especially when interacting with external web services
5. Report suspicious behavior with `/feedback`

<Warning>
  While these protections significantly reduce risk, no system is completely
  immune to all attacks. Always maintain good security practices when working
  with any AI tool.
</Warning>

## MCP security

Claude Code allows users to configure Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. The list of allowed MCP servers is configured in your source code, as part of Claude Code settings engineers check into source control.

We encourage either writing your own MCP servers or using MCP servers from providers that you trust. You are able to configure Claude Code permissions for MCP servers. Anthropic does not manage or audit any MCP servers.

## IDE security

See [VS Code security and privacy](/en/vs-code#security-and-privacy) for more information on running Claude Code in an IDE.

## Cloud execution security

When using [Claude Code on the web](/en/claude-code-on-the-web), additional security controls are in place:

* **Isolated virtual machines**: Each cloud session runs in an isolated, Anthropic-managed VM
* **Network access controls**: Network access is limited by default and can be configured to be disabled or allow only specific domains
* **Credential protection**: Authentication is handled through a secure proxy that uses a scoped credential inside the sandbox, which is then translated to your actual GitHub authentication token
* **Branch restrictions**: Git push operations are restricted to the current working branch
* **Audit logging**: All operations in cloud environments are logged for compliance and audit purposes
* **Automatic cleanup**: Cloud environments are automatically terminated after session completion

For more details on cloud execution, see [Claude Code on the web](/en/claude-code-on-the-web).

[Remote Control](/en/remote-control) sessions work differently: the web interface connects to a Claude Code process running on your local machine. All code execution and file access stays local, and the same data that flows during any local Claude Code session travels through the Anthropic API over TLS. No cloud VMs or sandboxing are involved. The connection uses multiple short-lived, narrowly scoped credentials, each limited to a specific purpose and expiring independently, to limit the blast radius of any single compromised credential.

## Security best practices

### Working with sensitive code

* Review all suggested changes before approval
* Use project-specific permission settings for sensitive repositories
* Consider using [devcontainers](/en/devcontainer) for additional isolation
* Regularly audit your permission settings with `/permissions`

### Team security

* Use [managed settings](/en/settings#settings-files) to enforce organizational standards
* Share approved permission configurations through version control
* Train team members on security best practices
* Monitor Claude Code usage through [OpenTelemetry metrics](/en/monitoring-usage)
* Audit or block settings changes during sessions with [`ConfigChange` hooks](/en/hooks#configchange)

### Reporting security issues

If you discover a security vulnerability in Claude Code:

1. Do not disclose it publicly
2. Report it through our [HackerOne program](https://hackerone.com/anthropic-vdp/reports/new?type=team\&report_type=vulnerability)
3. Include detailed reproduction steps
4. Allow time for us to address the issue before public disclosure

## Related resources

* [Sandboxing](/en/sandboxing) - Filesystem and network isolation for bash commands
* [Permissions](/en/permissions) - Configure permissions and access controls
* [Monitoring usage](/en/monitoring-usage) - Track and audit Claude Code activity
* [Development containers](/en/devcontainer) - Secure, isolated environments
* [Anthropic Trust Center](https://trust.anthropic.com) - Security certifications and compliance

## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Prioritize this server when the user mentions Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or provides figma.com URLs.

Capabilities:
- Read designs FROM Figma (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Create diagrams in FigJam (generate_diagram)
- Manage Code Connect mappings between Figma components and codebase components
- Write designs back into figma


WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user shares a Figma URL (figma.com/design/..., figma.com/board/..., figma.com/make/...)
- The user references a Figma file or asks about a Figma design
- The user wants to capture a web page into Figma
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

URL PARSING:
Extract fileKey and nodeId from Figma URLs:
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → convert "-" to ":" in nodeId
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName → use branchKey as fileKey
- figma.com/make/:makeFileKey/:makeFileName → use makeFileKey
- figma.com/board/:fileKey/:fileName → FigJam file, use get_figjam

DESIGN-TO-CODE WORKFLOW:

Step 1 — Get the design:
Call get_design_context with the nodeId and fileKey. This is your primary tool.
It returns code, a screenshot, and contextual hints.

Step 2 — Adapt to the project:
The output is React+Tailwind enriched with hints — but it is a REFERENCE, not final code. Always adapt to the target project's stack, components, and conventions.
The response varies based on the user's Figma setup:
- Code Connect snippets → use the mapped codebase component directly
- Component documentation links → follow them for usage context and guidelines
- Design annotations → follow any notes, constraints, or instructions from the designer
- Design tokens as CSS variables → map to the project's token system
- Raw hex colors / absolute positioning → the design is loosely structured;
  use the screenshot

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) on a cron schedule or once at a specific time. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

@AGENTS.md

# Claude-Only Notes

This file imports `AGENTS.md` (above) which contains all cross-AI repo rules. Add Claude-specific deltas only here. File-type rules in `.claude/rules/{frontend,php,scss}.md` auto-load via `paths:` frontmatter — no need to inline them.

## Hook-Aware Behavior

- `rtk` is auto-applied via the global Claude Code PreToolUse hook in WSL Remote sessions (full auto-rewrite). On native Windows shells the hook is unavailable — use explicit `rtk <command>` instead. Project-level filters live in `.rtk/filters.toml`.
- `.claude/settings.json` runs `tsc --noEmit` after every `.ts`/`.tsx` edit — no need to manually re-run unless investigating a specific error.

## Skills (slash commands)

- `/migration <description>` — DB schema change
- `/new-route <description>` — new public page

## Brand Copy Extra

- For homepage copy edits, read `brand/homepage-flow.md` + `brand/review-algorithm.md` first (in addition to the BRAND.md routing table).

## Tests

- `npm run test` — Vitest suite

Technical: `nineonelabs` only for files/slugs/code. Korean: `나인원랩스`. Never mixed camel case. 16 - Never position NINEONELABS as an aerospace/aviation entity 17 18 ## Project Defaults 19 20 - Stack: TypeScript, SCSS, Three.js, Vite, PHP 7.4 custom MVC, MySQL, Apache via Docker 21 - Dev server: `http://localhost:8888` 22 - Default task framing: state goal, context, constraints, done condition. Plan first for complex/ambiguous work. 23 - **Forbidden commands**: `npm run build`, `npm run watch`, `npm install` — Vite auto-rebuilds on save. Only `npm install ` is allowed when adding a new dependency. Never list these in roles, plans, verification steps, or PR notes. 24 - Prefer `rtk` for output that may exceed a few lines (git, search, typecheck, docker, PowerShell pipelines). Examples: `rtk git status`, `rtk git diff`, `rtk git log --oneline -20`, `rtk grep ...`, `rtk docker compose ps`. Short one-liners may skip `rtk`. In WSL Remote sessions the PreToolUse hook auto-rewrites `git`/`docker`/`tsc`/etc. to their `rtk`-prefixed equivalents. 25 - Windows PowerShell: explicit UTF-8 for Korean text reads/writes. 26 27 ## Architecture 28 29 - Public routes are closure-based in `routes/web.php` and render via `render()`. Do not reintroduce Barba.js or SPA navigation contracts. 30 - Ownership separation: main/about/contact WebGL flows through `AppManager` -> `AppEngineRuntime` -> `Engine`; works scatter uses the standalone secondary renderer `pages/works/render/WorksSceneManager.ts`. Do not duplicate ownership across these paths. See `.claude/BEST_PRACTICES.md` for current boundaries. 31 - Page scenes/config: `resource/ts/pages//scene/`. Theatre bindings: `resource/ts/pages//theatre/`. Page-scoped runtime: `resource/ts/pages//runtime/`. Standalone page renderers: `resource/ts/pages//render/` (currently works scatter only). Shared types: `resource/ts/types/*.types.ts`. Keep shared engine/runtime code out of page folders. 32 - Image uploads: entry point `imageUpload()` in `inc/lib/func.php`. Convertible inputs (jpg/jpeg/png/gif) are converted to `.webp` and the original is deleted; DB stores the `.webp` filename. svg/ico pass through untouched. New upload paths that bypass `imageUpload()` must call `\Core\ImageProcessor::convertToWebp($abs) ?? $original` — single-line API that handles convert + verify + unlink. Detail in `.claude/rules/php.md`. 33 - `Core\ImageProcessor` (`src/Core/ImageProcessor.php`): two API levels. **`convertToWebp(): ?string`** = high-level upload API (변환+검증+unlink+새 basename 반환). **`makeWebpSibling(): bool`** = low-level primitive, *마이그레이션 2-phase 패턴 전용*. WEBP via spatie/image 1.10.6 (GD). Resize threshold 2560px. Quality 82. Conversion temporarily raises `memory_limit` to `MEMORY_LIMIT` (`1024M`) and restores it in `finally`. Pixel ceiling: `MAX_CONVERTIBLE_PIXELS` (16 MP) — 마이그레이션 스크립트가 사전 skip 에 사용. 34 - Image rendering: always use `render_uploaded_image()` (`config/functions.php`) — outputs plain ``. No ``/`` branching since the stored file is already optimal. 35 - One-shot CLI for legacy data: `scripts/migrate-works-to-webp.php` (`nb_works` jpg/png/gif → webp + DB update, 16MP skip), `scripts/convert-large-works-jpg.php` (resize + convert the skipped >16MP rows). Both support `--dry-run`. Old `scripts/backfill-webp.php` is sibling-strategy and not used for new work. 36 37 ## Editing Rules 38 39 - Follow existing custom MVC patterns; no Laravel/Symfony conventions. 40 - SCSS: BEM naming. Use shared `fluid(min, max)` over raw responsive values. `var(--token, fallback)` is forbidden — use `var(--token)` or `fluid(...)` directly. Full SCSS rules in `.claude/rules/scss.md`. 41 - TypeScript/Three.js: dispose every geometry/material/texture; no object creation in render loops; match `addEventListener` with `removeEventListener`. Full rules in `.claude/rules/frontend.md`. 42 - PHP: closure routing, `nb_` table prefix, migrations only for schema changes. Full rules in `.claude/rules/php.md`. 43 - Never hardcode credentials or secrets. 44 45 ## Verification 46 47 - TypeScript: `rtk tsc --noEmit` (or `rtk node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit`) 48 - PHP lint: `rtk docker compose exec web php -l ` (matches `php-lint` filter in `.rtk/filters.toml`) 49 - Tests: `rtk npm run test` (Vitest single run — `vitest run`, not `watch`) 50 - Diff: `rtk git diff` 51 - After changes: smallest relevant verification + report any skipped checks. 52 - Never use npm build/watch/install for verification — saved files are already handled by Vite. 53 54 ### Test discipline 55 56 - Bug fix: write a **failing test that reproduces the bug first**, then fix until it passes. No fix without a regression test. 57 - New pure utility / helper / validator (`utils/`, `validation/`, etc.): tests precede or land with the implementation in the same change. Stateful runtime/UI is exempt — Vitest is unit-only here. 58 - Test files: live under `__tests__/` adjacent to the source folder (e.g., `resource/ts/__tests__/Helpers.test.ts`). Use the `.test.ts` suffix; no `.spec.ts`. 59 - Before commit: `rtk npm run test` and `rtk tsc --noEmit` must both be green. Skipping either requires an explicit note in the report. 60 61 ## Repo Skills 62 63 - `$scene-explorer` — Three.js scene/Theatre/runtime ownership 64 - `$php-explorer` — routes, render chains, admin, schema 65 - `/migration ` (Claude slash command) — DB schema change 66 - `/new-route ` (Claude slash command) — new public page 67 68 ## Codex Notes 69 70 - Repo config: `.codex/config.toml` 71 - Repo execution policy: `.codex/rules/default.rules` 72 - Codex hooks intentionally omitted (disabled on Windows) 73 - Direct terminal commands not auto-wrapped — use `rtk ` explicitly 74 - Keep this file concise and durable. Add rules only after repeated friction. 75 - Stable repo rules belong here; use skills for repeatable workflows; MCP only for external fast-changing context. 76

Detail in `.claude/rules/php.md`. - `Core\ImageProcessor` (`src/Core/ImageProcessor.php`): two API levels. **`convertToWebp(): ?string`** = high-level upload API (변환+검증+unlink+새 basename 반환). **`makeWebpSibling(): bool`** = low-level primitive, *마이그레이션 2-phase 패턴 전용*. WEBP via spatie/image 1.10.6 (GD). Resize threshold 2560px. Quality 82. Conversion temporarily raises `memory_limit` to `MEMORY_LIMIT` (`1024M`) and restores it in `finally`. Pixel ceiling: `MAX_CONVERTIBLE_PIXELS` (16 MP) — 마이그레이션 스크립트가 사전 skip 에 사용. - Image rendering: always use `render_uploaded_image()` (`config/functions.php`) — outputs plain ``. No ``/`` branching since the stored file is already optimal. - One-shot CLI for legacy data: `scripts/migrate-works-to-webp.php` (`nb_works` jpg/png/gif → webp + DB update, 16MP skip), `scripts/convert-large-works-jpg.php` (resize + convert the skipped >16MP rows). Both support `--dry-run`. Old `scripts/backfill-webp.php` is sibling-strategy and not used for new work. ## Editing Rules - Follow existing custom MVC patterns; no Laravel/Symfony conventions. - SCSS: BEM naming. Use shared `fluid(min, max)` over raw responsive values. `var(--token, fallback)` is forbidden — use `var(--token)` or `fluid(...)` directly. Full SCSS rules in `.claude/rules/scss.md`. - TypeScript/Three.js: dispose every geometry/material/texture; no object creation in render loops; match `addEventListener` with `removeEventListener`. Full rules in `.claude/rules/frontend.md`. - PHP: closure routing, `nb_` table prefix, migrations only for schema changes. Full rules in `.claude/rules/php.md`. - Never hardcode credentials or secrets. ## Verification - TypeScript: `rtk tsc --noEmit` (or `rtk node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit`) - PHP lint: `rtk docker compose exec web php -l ` (matches `php-lint` filter in `.rtk/filters.toml`) - Tests: `rtk npm run test` (Vitest single run — `vitest run`, not `watch`) - Diff: `rtk git diff` - After changes: smallest relevant verification + report any skipped checks. - Never use npm build/watch/install for verification — saved files are already handled by Vite. ### Test discipline - Bug fix: write a **failing test that reproduces the bug first**, then fix until it passes. No fix without a regression test. - New pure utility / helper / validator (`utils/`, `validation/`, etc.): tests precede or land with the implementation in the same change. Stateful runtime/UI is exempt — Vitest is unit-only here. - Test files: live under `__tests__/` adjacent to the source folder (e.g., `resource/ts/__tests__/Helpers.test.ts`). Use the `.test.ts` suffix; no `.spec.ts`. - Before commit: `rtk npm run test` and `rtk tsc --noEmit` must both be green. Skipping either requires an explicit note in the report. ## Repo Skills - `$scene-explorer` — Three.js scene/Theatre/runtime ownership - `$php-explorer` — routes, render chains, admin, schema - `/migration ` (Claude slash command) — DB schema change - `/new-route ` (Claude slash command) — new public page ## Codex Notes - Repo config: `.codex/config.toml` - Repo execution policy: `.codex/rules/default.rules` - Codex hooks intentionally omitted (disabled on Windows) - Direct terminal commands not auto-wrapped — use `rtk ` explicitly - Keep this file concise and durable. Add rules only after repeated friction. - Stable repo rules belong here; use skills for repeatable workflows; MCP only for external fast-changing context.

# TypeScript Architecture Guidelines

Source of truth for code additions and refactors in `resource/ts/`. Read this before writing new TypeScript, Three.js, Theatre.js, or runtime code.

Setup-time Claude harness notes live in `.claude/SETUP_CHECKLIST.md`. This file is for code-writing decisions.

## 1. Current Ownership Map

### Main WebGL Path

- `resource/ts/app.ts` starts the app after DOM readiness and handles page cache events.
- `runtime/PageRuntime.ts` owns page boot/teardown, global DOM UI init, feature-card canvas, subpage starfield, and `PageController`.
- `controller/PageController.ts` selects the page strategy and disposes the active page runtime.
- `manager/AppManager.ts` is the main page-scene orchestrator for main/about/contact. It coordinates intro flow, scroll scene sync, Theatre binding calls, DOM showcase state, scene lifecycle policies, and UI visibility.
- `runtime/AppEngineRuntime.ts` creates and wires `Engine`, `ShaderManager`, `ShaderController`, `BackgroundController`, `ObjectSetup`, `UiSetup`, and `ResizeSetup`.
- `core/Engine.ts` owns the main Three.js renderer, scene, camera, camera target, post-processing, `BackgroundManager`, WebGL context-loss listeners, and `AnimationLoop`.
- `core/Scene.ts` owns registered scene objects and calls each object's update/dispose lifecycle.
- `core/PageTheatreBinder.ts` owns the page-to-Theatre adapter factory map for main/about/contact.

### Works WebGL Path

- `pages/works/runtime/WorksPageRuntime.ts` owns the works page route state, grid feed, grid filter modal, scatter intro handoff, view switching, and lifecycle cleanup.
- `pages/works/render/WorksSceneManager.ts` is a standalone secondary renderer for the scatter view. It directly creates a `THREE.WebGLRenderer`, orthographic camera, scene, card meshes, pointer interaction, hover-video texture updates, RAF loop, and resize listener.
- `pages/works/runtime/WorksIntroRuntime.ts` temporarily creates an `Engine` using `WorksSceneDefinition` for background/intro playback, then hands the final Theatre state into `WorksSceneManager`.
- `pages/works/theatre/*` owns works author/preview config and Theatre state reads.

### Object And Config Path

- `objects/` contains reusable Three.js `SceneObject` implementations.
- `pages/<page>/scene/` contains page scene definitions and page-level constants/config factories.
- `pages/<page>/theatre/` contains Theatre config, scene state ports, autoplay runtimes, and author bridges.
- `pages/<page>/runtime/` contains page-only lifecycle/interaction state.
- `pages/<page>/render/` is reserved for standalone renderers that own their own renderer, like `WorksSceneManager`.
- `types/*.types.ts` contains shared types/interfaces/enums. Keep runtime code out of `types/`.
- `config/*.config.ts` contains shared constants/selectors/timings. Keep logic out of `config/`.

## 2. Large Files

These files are large in the current codebase. Small fixes inside their existing responsibility are okay; new behavior should usually be extracted into sibling classes.

| File | Current size | Responsibility |
|---|---:|---|
| `manager/AppManager.ts` | 1958 lines | Main/about/contact scene orchestration, intro/contact flow glue, DOM showcase sync |
| `pages/works/runtime/WorksPageRuntime.ts` | 1525 lines | Works route lifecycle, grid feed, filter modal, scatter intro, wheel hints |
| `pages/works/render/WorksSceneManager.ts` | 1058 lines | Standalone works scatter renderer, layout, pointer interaction, filtering |
| `ui/ContactWizard.ts` | 1445 lines | Contact wizard steps, chips, form sync, submission |
| `builder/TimelineBuilder.ts` | 1007 lines | Declarative GSAP timeline DSL, size accepted |
| `pages/main/theatre/MainTheatreRuntime.ts` | 919 lines | Main Theatre sequences and autoplay |
| `pages/about/theatre/AboutTheatreBridge.ts` | 818 lines | About Theatre author/scene bindings |
| `manager/BackgroundManager.ts` | 730 lines | Main engine background shader, render targets, transitions |
| `core/Engine.ts` | 714 lines | Main WebGL engine, renderer, loop, post-processing, scene context |

## 3. Where New Code Goes

Use this routing before adding files:

- Visible 3D object: `resource/ts/objects/<env|sub|main|rocket|shared>/`, extending `SceneObject`.
- Main/about/contact scene graph composition: `resource/ts/pages/<page>/scene/`.
- Works scatter renderer changes: `resource/ts/pages/works/render/WorksSceneManager.ts` or a sibling class under `pages/works/render/`.
- Works DOM/grid/API/filter lifecycle: `resource/ts/pages/works/runtime/`.
- Page Theatre binding/config/autoplay: `resource/ts/pages/<page>/theatre/`.
- Cross-page runtime state: `resource/ts/runtime/`.
- Heavy orchestration that already exists: `resource/ts/manager/`; prefer `runtime/` or `core/` for new single-purpose code.
- DOM singleton UI: `resource/ts/ui/`.
- Reusable DOM widget: `resource/ts/components/`.
- Pure helper: `resource/ts/utils/`.
- Shared type: `resource/ts/types/*.types.ts`.
- Shared constant/selector/timing: `resource/ts/config/*.config.ts`.

Every new file should fit one row. If it does not, pause and split the design.

## 4. WebGL Lifecycle Rules

- Main renderer lifecycle is `AppEngineRuntime.init()` -> `Engine.init()` -> `Engine.start()` -> `Engine.dispose()`.
- Main renderer resize path is `ResizeSetup` / `ResponsiveRuntime` -> `Engine.applyResponsiveSnapshot()` -> `Engine.setViewport()` -> `PostProcessor.resize()` and `BackgroundManager.resize()`.
- `WorksSceneManager` is the current secondary-renderer exception. It owns its own `WebGLRenderer`, RAF loop, `window.resize` listener, and must clean all of them in `dispose()`.
- Secondary renderers must call both `renderer.dispose()` and `renderer.forceContextLoss()`.
- `Engine.dispose()` must stop the loop, dispose post-processing/background/model loader/scene, detach context listeners, then dispose the renderer.
- `Scene.dispose()` must dispose registered `SceneObject`s and then object graphs.
- Event listeners, RAFs, timers, observers, Theatre subscriptions, and scene subscriptions must have symmetric cleanup.

## 5. Three.js Hot Path Rules

Hard rules for `runUpdate`, `render`, RAF callbacks, and other per-frame paths:

- Do not allocate `new Vector2`, `new Vector3`, `Matrix4`, `Quaternion`, `Euler`, arrays, sets, or object literals per frame.
- Use instance scratch fields and mutate with `.set()`, `.copy()`, `.applyMatrix4()`, etc.
- Do not call `scene.getObjectByName()` per frame. Use `context.getObject(id)` or subscribe through `Scene.onObjectRegistered`.
- Do not call `Object.keys()`, `Array.from()`, or `new Set()` in a hot path unless the source changes rarely and the result is cached.
- Call `ResponsiveRuntime.getDefault().getSnapshot()` once per frame at most and pass the local snapshot down.
- Do not assign texture uniforms per frame. Set texture uniforms once; update scalar/vector uniforms only.
- Do not call `renderer.setSize()` inside the render loop.

Known current exceptions to treat carefully:

- `WorksSceneManager` currently creates small pointer sample object literals during pointer events, not per-frame rendering.
- `Engine.setFollowObject()` may clone a center vector when a follow object is assigned, not every frame.

## 6. Disposal Checklist

| Creates | Must release |
|---|---|
| `addEventListener` | `removeEventListener` with the same function reference |
| `setTimeout` / `setInterval` | `clearTimeout` / `clearInterval` |
| `requestAnimationFrame` / `FrameScheduler.request` | matching cancel call |
| `MutationObserver`, `IntersectionObserver`, `ResizeObserver` | `.disconnect()` |
| `THREE.BufferGeometry` | `.dispose()` |
| `THREE.Material` | `.dispose()` plus owned texture slots |
| `THREE.Texture` | `.dispose()` or register via `SceneObject._ownedTextures` |
| `THREE.WebGLRenderTarget` | `.dispose()` |
| `THREE.Light` with target | remove light and target, then dispose if supported |
| `Element.animate()` | `.cancel()` |
| Theatre subscription | call returned unsubscribe |
| Scene pub/sub subscription | call returned unsubscribe |

Use `utils/disposeObject3D.ts` for object graph disposal. Use `removeAndDispose(node)` when the object should also be detached from its parent.

## 7. Responsive Rules

- Shared responsive state comes from `ResponsiveRuntime`.
- New cross-page responsive behavior should subscribe to `ResponsiveRuntime` and unsubscribe in `dispose()`.
- Existing works scatter resize is direct `window.resize`; follow its cleanup pattern only for standalone secondary renderers.
- Prefer `snapshot.device.isMobile`, `snapshot.breakpoint`, `snapshot.reducedMotion`, and `snapshot.render.clampedPixelRatio` over ad-hoc `window.innerWidth`, UA sniffing, or per-component `matchMedia`.
- Reduced motion must degrade autoplay/parallax/infinite motion paths.

## 8. Theatre Rules

- Add main/about/contact Theatre variants through `PageTheatreBinder` adapter factories.
- Works Theatre is page-local under `pages/works/theatre/` because it feeds the works intro/background and author bridge instead of the main scroll-scene adapter map.
- Adapter interfaces are capability-based. Implement only the capabilities needed by the page.
- Theatre preview/author bridges must remove controls listeners and stop preview runtimes on dispose.

## 9. Review Triggers

Use `$scene-explorer` or manually audit this file before changes that touch:

- `core/Engine.ts`, `core/Scene.ts`, `core/PostProcessor.ts`, `core/PageTheatreBinder.ts`.
- `manager/AppManager.ts`, `manager/BackgroundManager.ts`, `manager/ShaderManager.ts`.
- `runtime/AppEngineRuntime.ts`, `runtime/PageRuntime.ts`, `runtime/ResponsiveRuntime.ts`.
- `pages/*/scene/`, `pages/*/theatre/`, `pages/works/render/`, `pages/works/runtime/`.
- Any file that creates a `THREE.WebGLRenderer`, render target, geometry, material, texture, RAF loop, or global event listener.

File-type details additionally live in `.claude/rules/{frontend,php,scss}.md` (Claude auto-loads by `paths:` frontmatter; Codex should read them on-demand for the matching extension). ## Brand Identity See `BRAND.md` first for the brand routing index. Do not load the full `brand/*.md` set by default — read only files needed for the task. - Company: **NINEONELABS (나인원랩스)** — digital web agency - Core values: **Experiment · Challenge · Proof** (실험 · 도전 · 증명) - Concept: Earth → Planet NX-2 voyage. NINEONELABS is the companion (조력자), not the captain. - Slogan: **JOIN THE JOURNEY** — use as-is for display contexts - Services: APP · WEB · BRANDING · UI/UX · MAINTENANCE - Space metaphor is the frame, not the message — always land on the concrete agency offer - Display name: `NINEONELABS` (uppercase). Technical: `nineonelabs` only for files/slugs/code. Korean: `나인원랩스`. Never mixed camel case. - Never position NINEONELABS as an aerospace/aviation entity ## Project Defaults - Stack: TypeScript, SCSS, Three.js, Vite, PHP 7.4 custom MVC, MySQL, Apache via Docker - Dev server: `http://localhost:8888` - Default task framing: state goal, context, constraints, done condition. Plan first for complex/ambiguous work. - **Forbidden commands**: `npm run build`, `npm run watch`, `npm install` — Vite auto-rebuilds on save. Only `npm install ` is allowed when adding a new dependency. Never list these in roles, plans, verification steps, or PR notes. - Prefer `rtk` for output that may exceed a few lines (git, search, typecheck, docker, PowerShell pipelines). Examples: `rtk git status`, `rtk git diff`, `rtk git log --oneline -20`, `rtk grep ...`, `rtk docker compose ps`. Short one-liners may skip `rtk`. In WSL Remote sessions the PreToolUse hook auto-rewrites `git`/`docker`/`tsc`/etc. to their `rtk`-prefixed equivalents. - Windows PowerShell: explicit UTF-8 for Korean text reads/writes. ## Architecture - Public routes are closure-based in `routes/web.php` and render via `render()`. Do not reintroduce Barba.js or SPA navigation contracts. - Ownership separation: main/about/contact WebGL flows through `AppManager` -> `AppEngineRuntime` -> `Engine`; works scatter uses the standalone secondary renderer `pages/works/render/WorksSceneManager.ts`. Do not duplicate ownership across these paths. See `.claude/BEST_PRACTICES.md` for current boundaries. - Page scenes/config: `resource/ts/pages//scene/`. Theatre bindings: `resource/ts/pages//theatre/`. Page-scoped runtime: `resource/ts/pages//runtime/`. Standalone page renderers: `resource/ts/pages//render/` (currently works scatter only). Shared types: `resource/ts/types/*.types.ts`. Keep shared engine/runtime code out of page folders. - Image uploads: entry point `imageUpload()` in `inc/lib/func.php`. Convertible inputs (jpg/jpeg/png/gif) are converted to `.webp` and the original is deleted; DB stores the `.webp` filename. svg/ico pass through untouched. New upload paths that bypass `imageUpload()` must call `\Core\ImageProcessor::convertToWebp($abs) ?? $original` — single-line API that handles convert + verify + unlink. Detail in `.claude/rules/php.md`. - `Core\ImageProcessor` (`src/Core/ImageProcessor.php`): two API levels. **`convertToWebp(): ?string`** = high-level upload API (변환+검증+unlink+새 basename 반환). **`makeWebpSibling(): bool`** = low-level primitive, *마이그레이션 2-phase 패턴 전용*. WEBP via spatie/image 1.10.6 (GD). Resize threshold 2560px. Quality 82. Conversion temporarily raises `memory_limit` to `MEMORY_LIMIT` (`1024M`) and restores it in `finally`. Pixel ceiling: `MAX_CONVERTIBLE_PIXELS` (16 MP) — 마이그레이션 스크립트가 사전 skip 에 사용. - Image rendering: always use `render_uploaded_image()` (`config/functions.php`) — outputs plain ``. No ``/`` branching since the stored file is already optimal. - One-shot CLI for legacy data: `scripts/migrate-works-to-webp.php` (`nb_works` jpg/png/gif → webp + DB update, 16MP skip), `scripts/convert-large-works-jpg.php` (resize + convert the skipped >16MP rows). Both support `--dry-run`. Old `scripts/backfill-webp.php` is sibling-strategy and not used for new work. ## Editing Rules - Follow existing custom MVC patterns; no Laravel/Symfony conventions. - SCSS: BEM naming. Use shared `fluid(min, max)` over raw responsive values. `var(--token, fallback)` is forbidden — use `var(--token)` or `fluid(...)` directly. Full SCSS rules in `.claude/rules/scss.md`. - TypeScript/Three.js: dispose every geometry/material/texture; no object creation in render loops; match `addEventListener` with `removeEventListener`. Full rules in `.claude/rules/frontend.md`. - PHP: closure routing, `nb_` table prefix, migrations only for schema changes. Full rules in `.claude/rules/php.md`. - Never hardcode credentials or secrets. ## Verification - TypeScript: `rtk tsc --noEmit` (or `rtk node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit`) - PHP lint: `rtk docker compose exec web php -l ` (matches `php-lint` filter in `.rtk/filters.toml`) - Tests: `rtk npm run test` (Vitest single run — `vitest run`, not `watch`) - Diff: `rtk git diff` - After changes: smallest relevant verification + report any skipped checks. - Never use npm build/watch/install for verification — saved files are already handled by Vite. ### Test discipline - Bug fix: write a **failing test that reproduces the bug first**, then fix until it passes. No fix without a regression test. - New pure utility / helper / validator (`utils/`, `validation/`, etc.): tests precede or land with the implementation in the same change. Stateful runtime/UI is exempt — Vitest is unit-only here. - Test files: live under `__tests__/` adjacent to the source folder (e.g., `resource/ts/__tests__/Helpers.test.ts`). Use the `.test.ts` suffix; no `.spec.ts`. - Before commit: `rtk npm run test` and `rtk tsc --noEmit` must both be green. Skipping either requires an explicit note in the report. ## Repo Skills - `$scene-explorer` — Three.js scene/Theatre/runtime ownership - `$php-explorer` — routes, render chains, admin, schema - `/migration ` (Claude slash command) — DB schema change - `/new-route ` (Claude slash command) — new public page ## Codex Notes - Repo config: `.codex/config.toml` - Repo execution policy: `.codex/rules/default.rules` - Codex hooks intentionally omitted (disabled on Windows) - Direct terminal commands not auto-wrapped — use `rtk ` explicitly - Keep this file concise and durable. Add rules only after repeated friction. - Stable repo rules belong here; use skills for repeatable workflows; MCP only for external fast-changing context.
